tool_input.prompt:
You are fixing one confirmed regression on branch `fix/doctor-health-checks` in <repo> (PR #515). Do NOT push — commit and report; the leader pushes.

## The finding (Cursor Bugbot, verified by the leader before delegating)

`internal/doctor/doctor.go:445` — the executable-bit check:

```go
if statErr == nil && info.Mode().Perm()&0o111 == 0 {
    return Result{Name: name, Status: "FAIL", Detail: fmt.Sprintf("%s hook present but not executable — run: chmod +x %s", spec.ShortName, hook)}
}
```

This PR moved that check ahead of the sandbox call to fix qodo #3 (doctor was executing hooks git would never run). Correct fix on Unix. But it now also runs on Windows, where Go's `os.Stat` derives `FileMode` permission bits from the read-only attribute only — a regular file such as `.git/hooks/pre-commit` reports 0666 (writable) or 0444 (read-only), with no execute bits. So `Perm()&0o111 == 0` is true for EVERY hook on Windows.

Two consequences: every enabled Windows install FAILs with "present but not executable — run: chmod +x", which is unactionable there; and the unsupported-platform FAIL/WARN split added for qodo #12 at roughly doctor.go:483 becomes unreachable on Windows, because this returns first. Before this PR the exec-bit check sat after that branch and was unreachable on Windows, so this is a regression introduced by the branch itself.

CI is green because the doctor tests run on Linux. That is exactly the gap.

## Step 1 — verify before you change anything

Do not take my word or Bugbot's. Confirm Go's Windows `os.Stat` permission semantics from the actual Go source in your toolchain (`os/types_windows.go`, the `fileStat.Mode()` method) or official docs. Report what you found verbatim, including whether the version in this toolchain still has any `.exe`/`.bat`/`.cmd` special-casing. If the premise turns out false, STOP and report that instead of inventing a fix — a reviewer being wrong is a finding too, and two of the thirteen findings in the previous round on this PR were misattributed.

## Step 2 — fix

Gate the exec-bit check so it applies only where the bit is meaningful. Use the existing `sandboxGOOS` var (declared `internal/doctor/sandbox.go:49`, already used at sandbox.go:111 and overridden in tests) rather than reading `runtime.GOOS` inline — it is the established seam in this package and it is what makes the fix testable.

Preserve the qodo #3 property exactly: on platforms where the bit IS meaningful, no hook content may be executed before the exec-bit check returns FAIL. Do not solve this by moving the check back after the sandbox call.

Write a comment explaining WHY Windows is excluded — that the bit carries no execute semantics there, so the check cannot distinguish a runnable hook from a non-runnable one and would FAIL every install. Do not overclaim: state plainly that this means doctor cannot detect a genuinely non-runnable hook on Windows. This branch has spent an entire round removing comments that claimed more than the code delivers; do not add a new one.

## Step 3 — tests

Both arms, using the `sandboxGOOS` override the way `doctor_test.go:563-565` already does:
- `sandboxGOOS = "windows"`: a hook with no execute bits must NOT produce the exec-bit FAIL, and must reach the unsupported-platform FAIL/WARN split — assert on which of those two it lands in, so the test proves the split is actually reachable again.
- non-Windows: the exec-bit FAIL is preserved, and no execution occurs first (the existing witness-file technique from the #3 regression test).

Confirm the Windows-arm test FAILING against pre-fix code and paste the failure output in your report. A test for this that has never been observed red is worthless here.

## Step 4 — gates

- `make check` green, race enabled. Report BOTH the `ok` count and the `FAIL` count — a zero FAIL count alone cannot distinguish nothing-failed from nothing-ran. Pipe to a file with `tee`, never redirect.
- All five targets at exit 0: darwin/arm64, darwin/amd64, linux/arm64, linux/amd64 (the four `make dist` builds), plus windows/amd64 (build-verification only).
- No suppressions of any kind.

## Step 5 — docs

Add this to DES-077's addendum 3 as a finding fixed in this round, including the residual (no exec-bit-based detection on Windows, and still no Windows runtime testing — the guard is unit-tested through `sandboxGOOS`, not against a real Windows host). If the behavior change is user-facing, add a CHANGELOG entry under `[Unreleased]`.

Verify the addendum matches the code before you commit. In the previous round a docs commit's message claimed it had updated entries it never touched, and the leader caught the ADR contradicting its own diff — do not repeat that.

Scope is this one finding. Do not expand. Commit incrementally, each commit passing `make check`. Report what you fixed and anything you rejected with evidence.
